column1: Cinnamon is a sweet, fragrant spice produced from the inner bark of trees of the genus Cinnamomum, which is native to the Indian sub-continent.
column2: 肉桂是一种带甜香的香料，取自樟属树木的内层树皮。这类树原产于印度次大陆。

column1: It was known in biblical times, and is mentioned in several books of the Bible, both as an ingredient that was mixed with oils for anointing people’s bodies, and also as a token indicating friendship among lovers and friends.
column2: 圣经时代的人已经知道肉桂。《圣经》多卷书中都有提及：肉桂既可与油调和，用于涂抹身体的膏礼，也可作信物，表示恋人或朋友之间的情谊。
column4: books of the Bible|《圣经》各卷

column1: In ancient Rome, mourners attending funerals burnt cinnamon to create a pleasant scent.
column2: 在古罗马，参加葬礼的哀悼者会焚烧肉桂，让空气中散发好闻的香气。

column1: Most often, however, the spice found its primary use as an additive to food and drink.
column2: 不过，这种香料最常见、最主要的用途，还是添加到食物和饮料里。

column1: In the Middle Ages, Europeans who could afford the spice used it to flavour food, particularly meat, and to impress those around them with their ability to purchase an expensive condiment from the ‘exotic’ East.
column2: 中世纪买得起肉桂的欧洲人会拿它给食物调味，尤其是给肉类调味；他们也想借此让身边的人知道，自己买得起来自“异域”东方的昂贵调味品。

column1: At a banquet, a host would offer guests a plate with various spices piled upon it as a sign of the wealth at his or her disposal.
column2: 主人在宴会上会给宾客端上一盘堆满各色香料的盘子，以显示自己拥有多少可支配的财富。
column7: as a sign of|作为……的标志
column8: at his or her disposal|可由其支配

column1: Cinnamon was also reported to have health benefits, and was thought to cure various ailments, such as indigestion.
column2: 据说肉桂还有益健康，人们相信它能治疗多种病痛，例如消化不良。

column1: Toward the end of the Middle Ages, the European middle classes began to desire the lifestyle of the elite, including their consumption of spices.
column2: 中世纪末期，欧洲中产阶级开始向往上层阶级的生活方式，也想像他们那样消费香料。
column3: Toward the end of|接近……末期

column1: This led to a growth in demand for cinnamon and other spices.
column2: 于是，肉桂和其他香料的需求开始增长。

column1: At that time, cinnamon was transported by Arab merchants, who closely guarded the secret of the source of the spice from potential rivals.
column2: 当时，肉桂由阿拉伯商人运送，他们对香料产地严守秘密，防范潜在的竞争对手。

column1: They took it from India, where it was grown, on camels via an overland route to the Mediterranean.
column2: 他们用骆驼驮着肉桂，从它的种植地印度出发，经陆路运往地中海。

column1: Their journey ended when they reached Alexandria.
column2: 他们的旅程到了亚历山大港就结束了。

column1: European traders sailed there to purchase their supply of cinnamon, then brought it back to Venice.
column2: 欧洲商人乘船到那里购入所需的肉桂，再将它运回威尼斯。

column1: The spice then travelled from that great trading city to markets all around Europe.
column2: 这种香料随后从这座贸易重镇流向欧洲各地的市场。

column1: Because the overland trade route allowed for only small quantities of the spice to reach Europe, and because Venice had a virtual monopoly of the trade, the Venetians could set the price of cinnamon exorbitantly high.
column2: 陆路运输只能把少量肉桂送到欧洲，而威尼斯又几乎垄断了这门生意，所以威尼斯商人可以把肉桂定价定得极高。
column3: overland trade route|陆上贸易路线

column1: These prices, coupled with the increasing demand, spurred the search for new routes to Asia by Europeans eager to take part in the spice trade.
column2: 如此高的价格加上日益增长的需求，促使那些急于加入香料贸易的欧洲人去寻找通往亚洲的新路线。

column1: Seeking the high profits promised by the cinnamon market, Portuguese traders arrived on the island of Ceylon in the Indian Ocean toward the end of the 15th century.
column2: 15世纪末，葡萄牙商人为追逐肉桂市场许诺的丰厚利润，来到印度洋上的锡兰岛。
column8: toward the end of|在……即将结束时

column1: Before Europeans arrived on the island, the state had organized the cultivation of cinnamon.
column2: 欧洲人登岛之前，锡兰政权就已经在组织肉桂种植了。
column3: arrived on the island|来到岛上

column1: People belonging to the ethnic group called the Salagama would peel the bark off young shoots of the cinnamon plant in the rainy season, when the wet bark was more pliable.
column2: 萨拉伽马族人在雨季从肉桂的嫩枝上剥下树皮，因为此时湿润的树皮更柔韧。
column4: peel the bark off|剥下树皮

column1: During the peeling process, they curled the bark into the ‘stick’ shape still associated with the spice today.
column2: 他们在剥树皮的过程中把树皮卷成“棒”状，这仍是今天人们看到这种香料时熟悉的形状。

column1: The Salagama then gave the finished product to the king as a form of tribute.
column2: 萨拉伽马人随后把成品作为贡品献给国王。
column5: as a form of|作为……的一种形式

column1: When the Portuguese arrived, they needed to increase production significantly, and so enslaved many other members of the Ceylonese native population, forcing them to work in cinnamon harvesting.
column2: 葡萄牙人到来后需要大幅提高产量，便奴役了许多其他锡兰原住民，强迫他们采收肉桂。

column1: In 1518, the Portuguese built a fort on Ceylon, which enabled them to protect the island, so helping them to develop a monopoly in the cinnamon trade and generate very high profits.
column2: 1518年，葡萄牙人在锡兰修建了堡垒，使他们能够守卫这座岛，由此逐渐垄断肉桂贸易，攫取高额利润。
column6: develop a monopoly|逐步形成垄断

column1: In the late 16th century, for example, they enjoyed a tenfold profit when shipping cinnamon over a journey of eight days from Ceylon to India.
column2: 例如，16世纪后期，他们用八天从锡兰把肉桂运到印度，便能获得高达十倍的利润。
column6: journey of eight days|八天的行程

column1: When the Dutch arrived off the coast of southern Asia at the very beginning of the 17th century, they set their sights on displacing the Portuguese as kings of cinnamon.
column2: 17世纪伊始，荷兰人航行至南亚近海，便瞄准葡萄牙人在肉桂贸易中的霸主地位，想取而代之。
column4: at the very beginning of|在……之初
column5: set their sights on|把目标对准
column7: kings of cinnamon|肉桂贸易的霸主

column1: The Dutch allied themselves with Kandy, an inland kingdom on Ceylon.
column2: 荷兰人与锡兰内陆的康提王国结为同盟。

column1: In return for payments of elephants and cinnamon, they protected the native king from the Portuguese.
column2: 当地国王以大象和肉桂作酬劳，换取荷兰人的保护，以抵御葡萄牙人。

column1: By 1640, the Dutch broke the 150-year Portuguese monopoly when they overran and occupied their factories.
column2: 到1640年，荷兰人攻下并占领了葡萄牙人的商站，打破了葡萄牙长达150年的垄断。

column1: By 1658, they had permanently expelled the Portuguese from the island, thereby gaining control of the lucrative cinnamon trade.
column2: 到1658年，荷兰人已将葡萄牙人彻底逐出岛屿，从而掌控了利润丰厚的肉桂贸易。

column1: In order to protect their hold on the market, the Dutch, like the Portuguese before them, treated the native inhabitants harshly.
column2: 为了守住对市场的控制，荷兰人与先前的葡萄牙人一样，苛刻地对待岛上的原住民。
column3: protect their hold on|保住对……的控制

column1: Because of the need to boost production and satisfy Europe’s ever-increasing appetite for cinnamon, the Dutch began to alter the harvesting practices of the Ceylonese.
column2: 为了提高产量，满足欧洲人对肉桂不断增长的需求，荷兰人开始改变锡兰人采收肉桂的方法。

column1: Over time, the supply of cinnamon trees on the island became nearly exhausted, due to systematic stripping of the bark.
column2: 由于有计划地不断剥取树皮，岛上的肉桂树资源逐渐接近枯竭。

column1: Eventually, the Dutch began cultivating their own cinnamon trees to supplement the diminishing number of wild trees available for use.
column2: 最后，可供利用的野生肉桂树越来越少，荷兰人便开始自行栽种肉桂树加以补充。

column1: Then, in 1796, the English arrived on Ceylon, thereby displacing the Dutch from their control of the cinnamon monopoly.
column2: 1796年，英国人来到锡兰，取代了荷兰人对肉桂贸易的垄断。

column1: By the middle of the 19th century, production of cinnamon reached 1,000 tons a year, after a lower grade quality of the spice became acceptable to European tastes.
column2: 后来，欧洲消费者也能接受品质稍低的肉桂。到19世纪中叶，肉桂年产量已达到1000吨。
column3: middle of the 19th century|19世纪中叶
column8: European tastes|欧洲消费者的口味

column1: By that time, cinnamon was being grown in other parts of the Indian Ocean region and in the West Indies, Brazil, and Guyana.
column2: 到那时，印度洋地区的其他地方，以及西印度群岛、巴西和圭亚那，也都开始种植肉桂。

column1: Not only was a monopoly of cinnamon becoming impossible, but the spice trade overall was diminishing in economic potential, and was eventually superseded by the rise of trade in coffee, tea, chocolate, and sugar.
column2: 这时，垄断肉桂已变得不可能，整个香料贸易的经济潜力也在减弱，最终被日益兴盛的咖啡、茶、巧克力和糖贸易所取代。
